The current and original versions of two research documents were read after normal shutdown and reopen. The sample includes one explicitly addressed trashed item. Only child metadata was available for the PDF, HTML snapshot and PubMed link.

After native re-export, Core reopened both documents and returned the original exchange file for each format. Pandoc rendered an actual author-year citation. CSL JSON lost native library tags with this consumer. RIS kept 14 and 6 tags but provided no durable citation keys and the first date was read to year precision by Pandoc.

Core reopened the edited document history and returned documents with the supplied file entry keys. The paper's public group key, CSL ID and Bib entry key are distinct. Raw files retain fields outside the document projection; attachment files and library state are separate.

The externally edited title and incoming file citation key survived cold reads. Both prior AAOS version-2 documents were still present. Zotero's headless translator generated debat_how_2025 on external re-export of a file sent with debatHowGlobalSouth2025. AAOS retained the key actually received.
Two existing API originals and the two fixed document abstract blocks became research materials. A source-grounded knowledge candidate supported a local, unscored learning requirement and plan.
Four previous Core notes export under their original paths. Two edited bodies survive and the remaining two are byte-identical.
Obsidian 1.13.7 queries a real Albums Base and appends an embedded attachment link in the isolated Vault.
Four Markdown documents, the upstream Base and the PNG enter Core. The edited document is saved, read after restart and exported with five unchanged members.
A new Obsidian process reads both editors' changes, backlinks, attachment, tags, typed properties and the Albums view from the returned Vault.
The same album document at v4 exports its Chinese heading, two contiguous bold text nodes and an explicit hard break.
Official Obsidian reading mode rendered the Chinese H2, bold text and hard break. The native CLI inspected the displayed elements.
A 740,016-byte synthetic UTF-8 note exceeded the separate link-index budget. The prior Core workspace resumed at document v1 and exported the original bytes with an explicit link omission.
The six files from the prior formatted export were recognized as unchanged when paired. AAOS then saved two edits and authored one new note.
Obsidian 1.13.7 edited the artist and album through append and created a listening-session note through its CLI in an isolated Vault.
Independent changes and two new notes crossed in both directions. Different edits to the same album remained separately retrievable, including its native bytes. The PNG revision was captured.
Choosing the Vault album kept AAOS v5 readable and saved v6 on the same document. A cold replay skipped all eight files. The rebuilt Vault matched the eight selected files.
An independently launched Obsidian 1.13.7 read five changed or new notes from the rebuilt Vault and found the listening-session backlink.

Two byte-bound source quotes and a research package were read after restart. The real OpenMAIC worker built an exercise from the supplied question, options and answer key bound to album v6. After sync to v7 the activity kept historical v6 and zero attempts.

The renamed note kept its identity, the removed PNG remained in Core, the album heading kept its block ID, and choosing AAOS preserved the external artist variant. A read-only continuation checked all seven previously rebuilt files after a verifier path typo.

The exported seven-file Vault paired from its versioned receipt. The renamed note changed before pairing and advanced on the same document. Following a normal restart, sync without a receipt skipped all seven files without rewriting the cursor.

The verified 438,272-byte Core backup covered 14 sources. A formal restore to an empty directory retained the six current notes, both cited originals, the research package, the detached PNG, the captured alternative artist text and the historical exercise. Reusing the old cursor required a new connection.

In the formally restored workspace, a v4 catalog edit and six unchanged files reached the new seven-file Vault. An edit in that Vault advanced the listening-session document to v2, while the pre-restore Vault and cursor kept identical bytes.

The normal Core text job on an existing imported note reported six of nine headings and counted literal list/link/fence syntax. Image, quote and code-block counts were absent. The initial observer had queued this job and the continuation dispatched that same job.

The corrected Core worker reported the expected structure of nine public examples. Pandoc 3.10 read the same first 15 AST blocks and the one new paragraph from the AAOS v2 folder export. The original JPEG bytes were preserved.

A research document bound the original CommonMark image definition at byte offset 280, an edited-document block and the actual local JPEG. Both original sources were exported. Cold read returned an identical package.

Three public ENEX files yielded nine documents including separate same-title notes. A real PNG and SVG survived AAOS annotation and evernote2md 0.23.0 readback. The vendor illustration's missing image was reported. Reopening preserved v1 and v2.

Existing Core stored three names but indexed one. Native XML and the independent reader retained all three. The observer then stopped before creating research because the standalone MD5 also appeared in image recognition metadata.

New release Core read the existing v3 without rewriting it. All three source titles matched the production tag filter. A fixed document block, the ENEX image element and two original images entered the research package. A subsequent attempt to use a Vault route under a worker-free profile returned 404.

The generic folder importer ingested the independent reader's Markdown, PNG and SVG. The normal text worker returned the full annotated Markdown; all three files matched their source bytes. Cold Core read back the research package, image anchor and persisted v3.

Public ZIP yielded 24 editable pages, eight CSV snapshots and 34 immutable sources. The study page graph resolved eight edges including the original JPEG and parent collection source. The 13-column full CSV and eight-column view were distinct. Pandoc and a separate .NET CSV reader read AAOS changes, and a .NET ZIP edit returned to the same workspace. Two normal stops.

On the public Notion-format ZIP, the ordinary archive job produced 34 separately addressable content files with exact member paths and digests. It recorded 44 Finder records in the original archive. The registered 0.3.1 worker succeeded on attempt 2 of the existing failed job. Cold Core reread the full ZIP, the 34 children and the text of a formerly omitted note and table.

Six packaged clients operated on one workspace. The linked first receipt captures each command, including the first three-file Vault with a missing bibliography. On the updated release Core, two real Windows batch invocations imported and returned all four files byte for byte, with three resolved note links. Cold Core read nine previously saved documents across six sources. A test launcher and profile reused the retained Python and workers.

The Windows backend command imported 11 pinned official graph files as nine editable pages, 21 native UUIDs and 18 fixed relations. A UUID edit changed one line in one file. Independent mldoc reread it; an external edit returned with a nineteenth relation. Six acknowledged zero exits.

The live backup restored into a separate workspace. The initial native UUID and later edited version remained available. A text job grounded an excerpt; simulated admission connected it to a research export, course and six explicitly machine-generated unscored practice records. Thirteen reads matched on cold restart.
